renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Alpha diversity by habitat
  description: |-
    Each box summarises the samples of one habitat for one alpha-diversity metric, and each dot is a sample. It answers whether within-sample diversity differs between habitats.
    How to read: boxes that do not overlap point to habitats with different diversity, and a wide box means the samples of that habitat are heterogeneous. Shannon and Faith's PD grow with richness, and evenness says how equally the features share the reads. Compare with the beta-diversity ordination to see whether the same habitats also differ in composition.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  code: |-
    # reshape wide -> long so each metric becomes a facet panel (stays polars)
    df_modified = df.unpivot(
        index=["sample_id", "habitat"],
        on=["shannon", "observed_features", "faith_pd", "evenness"],
        variable_name="metric",
        value_name="value",
    )
  
    fig = px.box(
        df_modified,
        x="habitat", y="value", color="habitat",
        facet_col="metric", facet_col_wrap=2, points="all",
        category_orders={"metric": ["shannon", "observed_features", "faith_pd", "evenness"]},
        labels={"habitat": "Habitat", "value": "Value"},
    )
  
    fig.update_yaxes(matches=None)  # each panel keeps its own scale
    fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=")[-1]))
    fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend_title_text="Habitat", boxmode="group", margin=dict(t=10))

- component: card
  title: Shannon diversity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Shannon diversity over the samples in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how diverse a typical sample is, counting both richness and evenness.
    How to read: a higher value means more features and a more even share of the reads. A long whisker means samples differ a lot, so filter by habitat to see where. QIIME 2 publishes no pass or fail cut-off for this index.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  column: shannon
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Observed features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of distinct features (ASVs) observed per sample, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how rich a typical sample is.
    How to read: a high count means many distinct features were detected, but it depends on the sequencing depth, so read it together with the rarefaction curves. QIIME 2 publishes no pass or fail cut-off for this index.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  column: observed_features
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Faith's phylogenetic diversity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Faith's phylogenetic diversity per sample, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much of the phylogenetic tree a typical sample covers.
    How to read: a higher value means the features of the sample are spread over more distant lineages, not just more numerous. It needs a rooted tree, so it is absent from runs without one. QIIME 2 publishes no pass or fail cut-off.
    Sources: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/ and https://scikit.bio/docs/latest/generated/skbio.diversity.alpha.faith_pd.html
  column: faith_pd
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Evenness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Pielou's evenness per sample, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how equally the reads are shared between the features.
    How to read: values near 1 mean an even community and values near 0 a community dominated by few features. QIIME 2 publishes no pass or fail cut-off.
    Sources: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/ and https://scikit.bio/docs/latest/generated/skbio.diversity.alpha.pielou_e.html
  column: evenness
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Alpha-diversity table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its four alpha-diversity values and its metadata. It answers the exact value behind each box and dot.
    How to read: sort by a metric to find the least and most diverse samples, and compare outliers with their sequencing depth.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rarefaction_alpha
  title: Rarefaction curves
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: its Faith's phylogenetic diversity as the reads are subsampled to a growing depth, averaged over the iterations, with the spread of the iterations as a band. It answers whether the sequencing depth was enough to capture the diversity.
    How to read: a curve that levels out (approaches a slope of zero) means more reads would not reveal new diversity. A curve still climbing at the deepest depth means the diversity was not fully observed, or that sequencing error remains in the data. Choose the sampling depth for diversity analyses where most curves have levelled out, without dropping too many samples.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  kind: rarefaction
  config:
    show_ci: true
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    depth: depth
    metric: faith_pd
    iter: iter

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rarefaction_band
  title: Median rarefaction curves
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the median, over the iterations, of its Faith's phylogenetic diversity at each subsampling depth. It answers whether the diversity of each sample has stopped growing with depth.
    How to read: a line that levels out means more reads would not reveal new diversity, and a line still rising at the deepest depth means the sample was not sequenced deeply enough. Pick the sampling depth for diversity analyses where most lines have levelled out.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Sequencing depth (reads per sample)
    y_title: Faith's phylogenetic diversity
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: depth
    y: faith_pd

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rarefaction_curve
  title: Rarefaction by sample
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: its median Faith's phylogenetic diversity at each subsampling depth, with the controls of the rarefaction view. It answers which samples are the richest and whether their curves have levelled out.
    How to read: curves that flatten show that the diversity was captured, and the ordering of the curves shows which samples are richer at equal depth. A curve that stays steep is a sample worth resequencing or dropping from depth-sensitive comparisons.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  kind: rarefaction
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    depth: depth
    metric: faith_pd

- component: figure
  title: Rarefaction curves
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: its median Faith's phylogenetic diversity at each subsampling depth. It answers how fast the diversity of each sample grows with sequencing depth.
    How to read: hover a line to read the sample, and look for curves that level out. A curve still rising at the right edge was not sequenced deeply enough to see its full diversity.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: depth
    y: faith_pd
    color: sample
    labels:
      depth: Sequencing depth (reads per sample)
      faith_pd: Faith's phylogenetic diversity
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Faith's diversity along the curves
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Faith's phylogenetic diversity over every sample and depth step in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers the typical diversity reached across the rarefaction series.
    How to read: it mixes shallow and deep steps, so use it as a coarse summary and read the curves for the plateau. Filter to one sample to see its own range.
  column: faith_pd
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Subsampling depths
  description: |-
    The hero number is the deepest subsampling depth of the series, with the shallowest and the median step beside it. It answers how far the rarefaction explored.
    How to read: compare the deepest depth with the library sizes of the run, since a sampling depth above a library size would drop that sample.
  column: depth
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: deepest, shallowest and median depth

- component: table
  title: Rarefaction summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample at one subsampling depth, with its median diversity, the interquartile width over the iterations and the number of iterations. It answers the exact value behind each point of the curves.
    How to read: a wide interquartile width at a depth means the subsamples disagree, which usually happens at the shallowest steps.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: volcano
  title: Differential abundance volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a taxon in one contrast: its ANCOM-BC log fold change on the horizontal axis and its q-value (adjusted p-value) on the vertical axis, coloured by contrast. It answers which taxa differ most between the groups, in which direction, and how confidently.
    How to read: taxa in the upper left and upper right corners are less and more abundant than in the reference group, with high confidence. A cloud with almost nothing past the lines means little differential signal. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled taxa.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the q-value cut-off of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute effect size of 1. Both are the nf-core/ampliseq defaults for its differential-abundance barplot.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log fold change
    significance_label: -log10 q-value
  roles:
    feature_id: id
    effect_size: lfc
    significance: q_val
    label: Phylum
    category: contrast

- component: advanced_viz
  id: da_barplot
  title: Top changed taxa per contrast
  description: |-
    Each bar is a taxon: its ANCOM-BC log fold change in a contrast, for the taxa with the largest absolute change. It answers which taxa drive each contrast and in which direction.
    How to read: long bars to the right are more abundant than in the reference group and bars to the left less abundant; bars are marked when their q-value passes the cut-off. A large change without significance usually means a rare or variable taxon, so open the MA plot and the table to check it.
    Lines and annotations: significance is marked at a q-value below 0.05, the nf-core/ampliseq default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log fold change
  roles:
    feature_id: id
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: lfc
    significance: q_val
    label: Phylum

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qq
  title: P-value QQ plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a taxon: its observed raw p-value, as minus log10, against the value expected if no taxon differed between the groups. One trace is drawn per contrast. It answers whether the test statistics are well calibrated.
    How to read: points hugging the diagonal for most of the range and lifting off at the far end mean a few real signals over a calibrated null. A curve that leaves the diagonal early points to strong group structure or to a model that does not fit. Compare the contrasts and the ordination when one curve differs.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, the expectation when p-values are uniformly distributed under no effect. The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval of that null, so points inside it are consistent with chance.
  kind: qq
  config:
    show_ci: true
    show_identity: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    p_value: p_val
    category: contrast
    feature_id: id

- component: card
  title: Significant taxa by contrast
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of taxon calls with a q-value below 0.05, and the bars rank the contrasts by how many they hold. It answers which comparison shows the strongest differential signal.
    How to read: a contrast with many calls separates its groups clearly, and one with none shows no detectable difference. The count beside the hero is the number of distinct taxa behind the calls.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: contrast
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('significant')
  caption: calls, by contrast

- component: card
  title: Significant calls by kingdom
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of taxon calls with a q-value below 0.05, and the ring splits them by kingdom. It answers whether the differential signal sits in bacteria, archaea or both.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one kingdom says where the groups differ. Calls are counted per contrast, so a taxon significant in two contrasts counts twice.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: Kingdom
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('significant')
  caption: calls, by kingdom

- component: card
  title: Median q-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median q-value over every taxon and contrast in view, shown against the 0.05 cut-off. It answers whether a typical taxon differs between the groups.
    How to read: a median below the cut-off means most taxa differ, which is unusual outside strongly structured habitats. The smallest and largest q-values are listed beside it.
    Lines and annotations: the marker is the q-value of 0.05 used by nf-core/ampliseq as the ANCOM-BC significance level.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: q_val
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: median, against the 0.05 cut-off

- component: card
  title: Fold change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of ANCOM-BC log fold changes over every taxon and contrast in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the differences are overall.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most taxa are unchanged and a few change a lot. A median would cancel the two directions, so the range is shown instead. Filter to one contrast to compare them.
  column: lfc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: range, with the quartiles

- component: table
  title: Differential abundance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon in one contrast, with its log fold change, standard error, test statistic, p-value, q-value and whether the call is significant. It answers the exact estimate behind each point of the plots.
    How to read: sort by q-value to list the strongest calls, and filter on the significant column to keep the calls only.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: distance_heatmap
  title: Sample distances
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between two samples, computed from their relative abundances. It answers which samples have similar communities and which groups they form.
    How to read: dark blocks along the diagonal are groups of similar samples and the dendrograms show how they cluster. Samples that sit far from every other sample have an unusual community, so check them against the ordination and the habitat metadata.
    Note: Bray-Curtis runs from 0 for identical communities to 1 for communities that share nothing.
    Sources: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/ and https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.spatial.distance.braycurtis.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    cluster_rows: true
    cluster_cols: true
    normalize: none
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Distance matrix
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and each column the Bray-Curtis dissimilarity to another sample. It answers the exact distance between any two samples.
    How to read: read across a row to find the nearest and the most distant samples of the one in view.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: abundance_heatmap
  title: Taxon abundance by sample
  description: |-
    Each cell is the relative abundance of a taxon in a sample, scaled per taxon so that rows are comparable. It answers which taxa rise and fall together across the samples and which samples share a profile.
    How to read: blocks of the same colour across neighbouring samples are taxa that characterise those samples, and the dendrograms group similar taxa and samples. The side strip shows the kingdom of each taxon. A sample that clusters apart has an unusual community, so check it against the habitat metadata.
    Note: values are z-scored per row, so a colour compares a sample with the other samples for the same taxon, not one taxon with another.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    cluster_rows: true
    cluster_cols: true
    normalize: row_z
  roles:
    index: Phylum
    row_annotation_cols:
    - Kingdom

- component: advanced_viz
  id: embedding
  title: Samples on the first two axes
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample, placed by a principal coordinates analysis of the Bray-Curtis dissimilarities between samples. It answers whether samples of the same habitat or condition have similar communities.
    How to read: points that sit close have similar communities and points far apart differ. Groups that separate along the first axis carry the main source of variation. A sample far from its group is worth checking for a technical problem.
    Note: the axes are ordination coordinates, so their sign and scale have no absolute meaning.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PCo
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2

- component: table
  title: Ordination coordinates
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its coordinates on the first axes. It answers the exact position of each point.
    How to read: sort by an axis to find the samples at its two extremes.

- component: card
  title: Spread on the first axis
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of the samples along the first ordination axis, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far apart the samples are on the main axis of variation.
    How to read: a wide range with a box split into two clusters points to groups with distinct communities. The axis is centred, so its median says nothing.
  column: dim_1
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: range, with the quartiles

- component: card
  title: Spread on the second axis
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of the samples along the second ordination axis, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how much variation the second axis adds.
    How to read: a range much narrower than the first axis means one gradient explains most of the difference between samples.
  column: dim_2
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: range, with the quartiles

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ma_plot
  title: Fold change against mean abundance
  description: |-
    Each point is a taxon in one contrast: its mean abundance across samples on the horizontal axis (log10 of the count plus one) and its ANCOM-BC log fold change on the vertical axis. It answers whether the changes are real or only come from rare taxa.
    How to read: a flat cloud centred on zero with the significant taxa spread over abundance levels is healthy. A funnel that widens towards low abundance is the normal noise of rare taxa. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled taxa.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal lines mark an absolute effect size of 1, the nf-core/ampliseq default for its differential-abundance barplot.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/ampliseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: ma
  config:
    fold_change_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log fold change
    intensity_label: Mean abundance (log10 of count plus 1)
  roles:
    feature_id: feature_id
    avg_log_intensity: avg_log_intensity
    log2_fold_change: log2_fold_change

- component: table
  title: Fold change and abundance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon in one contrast, with its mean abundance, log fold change and q-value. It answers the exact values behind each point.
    How to read: sort by q-value to list the strongest calls, then compare their abundance in the plot.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rarefaction
  title: Rarefaction curves
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: its alpha diversity as the reads are subsampled to a growing depth, averaged over the iterations, with their spread as a band. The tab strip switches between Shannon, observed features and Faith's PD. It answers whether the sequencing depth was enough to capture the diversity.
    How to read: a curve that levels out (approaches a slope of zero) means more reads would not reveal new diversity. A curve still climbing at the deepest depth means the diversity was not fully observed, or that sequencing error remains in the data. Choose the sampling depth for diversity analyses where most curves have levelled out.
    Source: https://docs.qiime2.org/2024.10/tutorials/moving-pictures/
  kind: rarefaction
  config:
    metric_options:
    - shannon
    - observed_features
    - faith_pd
    show_ci: true
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    depth: depth
    metric: shannon
    iter: iter

- component: advanced_viz
  id: sunburst
  title: Kingdom and phylum composition
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon: the inner ring is the kingdom and the outer ring the phylum, sized by relative abundance summed over the samples in view and coloured by phylum. It answers which lineages make up the communities.
    How to read: a wide arc is a dominant lineage, and a ring made of many thin arcs is a diverse one. Click an arc to zoom in on it, and filter by habitat to compare groups.
    Note: unclassified reads form their own arc, so a large one points to a database or classification limit rather than a real group.
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: Phylum
  roles:
    ranks:
    - Kingdom
    - Phylum
    abundance: rel_abundance

- component: card
  title: Dominant relative abundance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest relative abundance of any taxon in any sample in view, with the median and the upper quartile beside it. It answers how dominant the leading taxon is.
    How to read: a large maximum against a small median is the usual shape of a community with a few dominant taxa and a long tail. Filter by sample or habitat to see how the dominance changes.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: largest, median and upper quartile

- component: card
  title: Taxa by kingdom
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct taxa detected, and the bars rank the kingdoms by how many detections they hold. The count beside it is the number of sample and taxon detections. It answers how many lineages the run recovered and where they come from.
    How to read: a run dominated by one kingdom is usual for a 16S survey. A high count of detections against a low count of taxa means the same taxa are found in many samples.
  column: taxonomy
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: Kingdom
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: detections, by kingdom
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Abundance of the leading phyla
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean relative abundance of a detected taxon, and the bars rank the phyla by their mean. The largest value is listed beside it. It answers which phyla are abundant when they are present.
    How to read: phyla at the top make up most of the reads where they occur. Only detections above zero are counted, so a phylum found in a single sample can still rank high. Unclassified taxa are left out.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: Phylum
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('Phylum') != 'Unclassified'
  caption: mean abundance when detected, by phylum

- component: table
  title: Relative abundance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon in one sample, with its relative abundance, its kingdom and phylum and the sample metadata. It answers the exact abundance behind each arc and card.
    How to read: sort by abundance to find the dominant taxa of a sample, or filter on a phylum to follow it across samples.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stacked_taxonomy
  title: Taxonomic composition per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the taxa of the chosen rank by their relative abundance, with the least abundant lumped into Other. It answers how the community composition differs between samples.
    How to read: bars with the same colour pattern are samples with similar communities, and a bar dominated by one colour is a sample with a dominant taxon. Switch the rank to move from phyla to genera, sort the samples, and hide parts from the controls.
    Note: unclassified reads form their own part, so a large one points to a database or classification limit.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: Phylum
    top_n: 12
    value_title: Relative abundance
    rank_label: Taxonomic rank
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: advanced_viz
  id: sunburst_taxonomy
  title: Taxonomic hierarchy
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon: rings run from kingdom outwards through the ranks the run holds, sized by relative abundance summed over the samples in view and coloured by phylum. It answers which lineages make up the communities and how they divide into finer groups.
    How to read: a wide arc is a dominant lineage, and its outer arcs show how it splits into classes, orders, families and genera. Click an arc to zoom in on it, and filter by sample to compare communities.
    Note: unclassified reads form their own arcs at each rank, so a large one points to a database or classification limit rather than a real group.
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: Phylum
  roles:
    abundance: abundance

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stacked_taxonomy_barplot
  title: Taxa barplot
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the taxa of the chosen rank by their relative abundance, with the least abundant lumped into Other. It answers how the community composition differs between samples.
    How to read: bars with the same colour pattern are samples with similar communities, and a bar dominated by one colour is a sample with a dominant taxon. Switch the rank to move from phyla to genera, and sort the samples from the controls.
    Note: unclassified reads form their own part, so a large one points to a database or classification limit.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: Phylum
    top_n: 12
    value_title: Relative abundance
    rank_label: Taxonomic rank
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: figure
  title: Reads per sample by phylum
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, stacked by phylum, with its height the number of reads assigned to each. It answers how many reads each sample holds and which phyla they belong to.
    How to read: bars of very different height are samples with different sequencing depth, so compare compositions on the relative abundance tab rather than here. A phylum that fills a bar dominates that sample.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: count
    color: Phylum
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      count: Read count
      Phylum: Phylum

- component: table
  title: Taxon counts table
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon in one sample, with its read count, kingdom and phylum and the sample metadata. It answers the exact count behind each bar segment.
    How to read: sort by count to find the dominant taxa, or filter on a phylum to follow it across samples.

- component: table
  title: Abundance matrix
  description: |-
    Each row is a taxon and each column a sample, holding the relative abundance of the taxon in that sample. It answers the exact abundance behind the clustered heatmap.
    How to read: read across a row to follow a taxon over the samples, and down a column to see what a sample is made of.

- component: card
  title: Classified ASVs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct ASVs that received a taxonomic assignment, and the count beside it is the number of rows. It answers how many sequence variants the classifier labelled.
    How to read: the two numbers match when every ASV has a single assignment, so a gap means some sequence variants appear in more than one row.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: uniqueness
  caption: distinct ASVs, against all rows

- component: card
  title: Classifier confidence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median classifier confidence over the ASVs in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how certain the taxonomic assignments are.
    How to read: values close to 1 are firm assignments, and a long lower whisker is a set of ASVs assigned with little support. The classifier only keeps an assignment at a rank when its confidence reaches the minimum set for the run, 0.7 by default, so the lowest values sit near that floor.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qiime2/q2-feature-classifier/master/q2_feature_classifier/classifier.py
  column: confidence
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: ASV taxonomy table
  description: |-
    Each row is an ASV with its assigned taxon, its ranks from kingdom to species, the classifier confidence and the habitat where it is most abundant. It answers what each sequence variant was called.
    How to read: sort by confidence to find the weakest assignments, and look at empty rank cells to see where the classifier stopped.

- component: card
  title: ASVs by phylum
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct ASVs with a phylum assignment, and the bars rank the phyla by how many ASVs they hold. It answers which phyla are the most diverse.
    How to read: the leading phyla hold most of the sequence variants. ASVs without a phylum are left out, so the number is below the total when some stay unclassified.
  column: taxon
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: Phylum
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('Phylum') != ''
  caption: ASVs, by phylum

- component: card
  title: Reached genus
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of ASVs with a genus assignment, shown as the share of all ASVs, and the count beside it is the number of distinct genera. It answers how deep the classification reaches.
    How to read: a low share is common for environmental samples, where many sequences have no close relative in the reference database. Compare with the phylum card to see where the classifier stops.
  column: Genus
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: completeness
  caption: ASVs classified to genus

- component: card
  title: Genus concentration
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genera, and the strip shows how much of the classified ASVs the leading genera hold. It answers whether a few genera dominate.
    How to read: a high share in the first genera means a narrow set of genera accounts for most variants, and a flat strip means a diverse set. ASVs without a genus are left out.
  column: Genus
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: Genus
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: pl.col('Genus') != ''
  caption: ASVs held by the leading genera
